newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin appeals to Gore over Galkin case.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin appeals to Gore over Galkin case.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin appealed to U.S. Vice President Al Gore on Thursday to limit damage to relations between Washington and Moscow from the case of arrested former spy Vladimir Galkin.
Chernomyrdin's spokesman Viktor Konnov told Interfax news agency the Galkin case was among subjects discussed in a telephone conversation between Gore and Chernomyrdin.
"We do not want this problem blown up any more," Konnov quoted Chernomyrdin as saying. The call took place before all charges against Galkin were dropped at a court in Worcester, Massachusetts.
Konnov quoted Gore as telling Chernomyrdin he would look into the case, which he described as probably a misunderstanding.
Russian intelligence officials protested vigorously against Galkin's arrest, describing it as a violation of unwritten understandings on how ex-agents should be treated.

The 50-year-old former spy, who did not conceal his past occupation on a visa application, was arrested by FBI agents on October 29 at John F. Kennedy airport in New York and accused of trying to steal secrets of the U.S. Strategic Defence Initiative.
